First public release.

autobones draws skeleton loaders from your real UI. It measures the text lines, images, avatars, buttons and cards you already rendered, and draws matching skeleton bones over them. Change the component and the skeleton changes with it.

## Highlights

- Works with **React, Vue, Svelte, Web Components and plain JS**, over one shared engine
- **Layout memory:** name a skeleton and it remembers the real shape, so later loads need no placeholder data
- **Ship layouts** captured in development, so first-time visitors get an exact skeleton too
- **No flicker:** `delay`, `minDuration` and a cross-fade into the content
- **Accessible:** `aria-busy`, `inert` content, and no animation under reduced motion
- Light and dark themes, with CSS variables for colors
- About 5 KB gzipped, zero dependencies, ESM and CJS builds with TypeScript types
- React: `<Skeleton>` with `ref` forwarding, the `useSkeleton` hook, and `"use client"` for Next.js

## Install

```bash
npm install autobones
```

## Links

- Live demo: https://autobones.netlify.app
- Docs: see the [README](https://github.com/Drinor101/autobones#readme)

## Known limits

- Tested by hand in Chrome. Firefox and Safari are not verified yet.
- The Vue and Svelte adapters are smoke-tested, with full example projects still to come.
- There is no automated test suite yet.
- With server-side rendering, the real content shows briefly before the skeleton takes over on hydration.
